1.title: Identity Protection and Governance
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Identity Protection and Governance. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft Entra. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe Microsoft Entra I D Governance. Describe access reviews. Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. Describe Microsoft Entra I D Protection. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft Entra (twenty-five to thirty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Four tools, four jobs
1.text: Four tools, four jobs. Microsoft Entra I D Governance. Job in one line: Make sure the right people have the right access for the right time. Question it answers: Who should have access, and for how long? Access reviews. Job in one line: Regularly re-check who has access and remove what is not needed. Question it answers: Do they still need it?

1.title: Four tools, four jobs, continued
1.text: Four tools, four jobs. Privileged Identity Management (P I M). Job in one line: Give privileged roles just in time, not permanently. Question it answers: Can administrators be admins only when needed? Microsoft Entra I D Protection. Job in one line: Detect and respond to identity risks. Question it answers: Is this sign-in or user risky?

1.title: Four tools, four jobs, continued
1.text: Four tools, four jobs. The figure shows this: Governance decides who gets access, P I M limits privilege, access reviews clean up, I D Protection detects risk.

1.title: Microsoft Entra ID Governance
1.text: Microsoft Entra I D Governance. I D Governance manages the identity and access life cycle at scale, balancing security and productivity. It adds capabilities to Entra I D. for licensing. Entitlement management. Bundles resources into access packages that users request, with approval and expiry. Lifecycle workflows. Automates joiner, mover and leaver tasks (create, change, remove access). Access reviews. Periodically confirm or remove access. Privileged Identity Management. Just-in-time, time-bound privileged access. Terms of use. Require users to accept terms before access. Exam tip: Joiner, mover, leaver equals lifecycle workflows. Access packages (a bundle of access that expires) equals entitlement management.

1.title: Access reviews
1.text: Access reviews. An access review lets the right people confirm whether access is still needed. What can be reviewed. Group memberships, application access, Entra and Azure roles, access packages. Reviewers. Resource owners, managers, the users themselves, or selected reviewers. Frequency. One time or recurring (monthly, quarterly, yearly). Outcome. Approve or deny; access can be removed automatically when the review ends. Why. Fights privilege creep and stale access and supports compliance and audits.

1.title: Access reviews, continued
1.text: Access reviews. The figure shows this: An access review cycle: schedule, reviewers decide, access removed or kept, results recorded. Exam tip: "Periodically verify that group members still need access" equals access review. It removes excess access; it does not detect risky sign-ins (that is I D Protection).

1.title: Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
1.text: Privileged Identity Management (P I M). P I M manages, controls and monitors access to important resources: Entra roles, Azure roles and groups. Just-in-time (J I T) access. Privileges are activated only when needed. Time-bound access. Roles expire after a set time. Eligible versus active. Eligible equals can activate the role; active equals has it now. Approval. Activation can require approval. M F A on activation. Require M F A to activate. Justification and notifications. Users give a reason; admins get alerts. Audit history and reviews. Every activation is logged; access reviews of roles.

1.title: Privileged Identity Management (PIM), continued
1.text: Privileged Identity Management (P I M). P I M reduces standing privilege: an attacker who steals an eligible admin's password still cannot use the role without activation. P I M needs Entra I D P two (or I D Governance). Exam tip: P I M equals just-in-time, time-limited admin rights. The key word is eligible: the person can become admin, but is not admin all the time.

1.title: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
1.text: Microsoft Entra I D Protection. I D Protection uses machine learning and Microsoft's threat data to detect identity risks, report them and automate responses. It needs Entra I D P two. User risk. The account may be compromised (for example leaked credentials). Sign-in risk. This sign-in may not be the real user (for example anonymous I P address, atypical or impossible travel, unfamiliar sign-in properties, password spray). Responses: risk-based Conditional Access policies can require M F A for risky sign-ins and a password change for risky users; admins can investigate, confirm or dismiss risks in reports. Exam tip: User risk equals account (leaked credentials). Sign-in risk equals this login (impossible travel). I D Protection detects; Conditional Access acts on the risk.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants administrators to be admins only when they need to do admin work, for a limited time. Which tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Privileged Identity Management. P I M gives just-in-time, time-bound privileged access.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Each quarter, managers must confirm that group members still need access. Which capability does this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Access reviews. Access reviews periodically confirm or remove access.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A sign-in comes from an anonymous I P address and an unusual location. Which tool classifies this as risky? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Microsoft Entra I D Protection. I D Protection detects risky sign-ins and users.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A user's credentials appear in a leaked list. Which risk type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: User risk. Leaked credentials indicate that the account may be compromised, which is user risk.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. In P I M, what does "eligible" mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The user can activate the role when needed. Eligible users must activate the role before using it.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. New employees, movers and leavers should get and lose access automatically as part of their life cycle. Which capability fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Lifecycle workflows in I D Governance. Lifecycle workflows automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does I D Governance manage? Answer: The identity and access life cycle: the right access for the right people for the right time. Question two. What can an access review check? Answer: Group memberships, application access, roles and access packages. Question three. What does P I M stand for? Answer: Privileged Identity Management.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between eligible and active in P I M? Answer: Eligible can activate the role; active has it now. Question five. Name the two risk types in I D Protection. Answer: User risk and sign-in risk. Question six. Which license level do P I M and I D Protection need? Answer: Microsoft Entra I D P two (or I D Governance for P I M).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. I D Governance: entitlement management (access packages), lifecycle workflows (joiner, mover, leaver), access reviews, P I M, terms of use. Access reviews: periodic; reviewers owners, managers, users; approve or deny; auto-remove access. P I M: just-in-time, time-bound, eligible versus active, approval, M F A on activation, audit; P two. I D Protection: detects user risk (leaked credentials) and sign-in risk (impossible travel, anonymous I P). In the next module, we continue the course.
